channel.title: Science News – Bias and Credibility - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Science News – Bias and Credibility (sciencenews.org)

item.title: Long nails don’t work on touchscreens. An experimental polish could help
item.description: Proton movement in the nail polish probably activates the touchscreen, but the formula isn’t ready to hit shelves yet.

item.title: Female giant rainforest mantises grow up to strike harder than males
item.description: Scientists tracked mantis strike force from youth to adulthood, showing females eventually hit far harder than males. Why is a mystery.

item.title: In a rare event, the moon got a massive new crater
item.description: A crater as wide as two American football fields formed in spring 2024, a size expected roughly once a century. A NASA orbiter got to watch.

item.title: Neandertals made antibacterial ointment, but may not have known it
item.description: A team of scientists re-created the way Neandertals made birch tar and found its antibacterial properties could fight off skin infections.

item.title: These insects fly with their legs. Physics explains how
item.description: Phantom crane flies change the angle of their splayed legs to increase or reduce drag, helping them navigate varying winds.

item.title: Watch the first video of a sperm whale birth captured by scientists
item.description: In a sperm whale birth recorded in more intimate detail than ever before, local whales huddled around the mother and lifted the calf to the surface.

item.title: A rare star in a tiny galaxy preserves a record of the early universe
item.description: Found in an ultrafaint dwarf galaxy, the ancient star’s unusual chemistry indicates it formed from gas enriched by a single early supernova.

item.title: Why AI agent teams often fail to work together
item.description: AI agents are starting to work in teams, but without careful organization, groups of bots can easily fall into chaos.

item.title: How snakes defy gravity to stand tall
item.description: Limbless tree snakes can lift most of their body into the air without toppling. They manage this by focusing all their bending forces at their base.

item.title: Quantum physics can confirm where someone is located
item.description: The concept of entanglement links far-flung particles. That relationship can prove that someone is in the location they claim to be.

item.title: Heavy tilling can leave land susceptible to floods, droughts
item.description: The tiny seismic signals of rainwater moving through the ground show how heavy tilling damage soil.

item.title: Secrets of the Bees zooms in on life in a hive
item.description: A new documentary available on Disney+ and Hulu appeals to our sense of wonder to highlight why bees need saving.

item.title: A comet may have flipped its spin and entered a death spiral
item.description: Gases jetting out of Comet 41P/Tuttle-Giacobini-Kresák may have caused it to reverse its spin in 2017, possibly leading to its eventual destruction.

item.title: Pronatalists want more babies. Their solutions aren’t rooted in science
item.description: Conservative pronatalists want a return to the traditional nuclear family. But that family structure is at odds with how humans evolved.

item.title: Just 10,000 quantum bits might crack internet encryption schemes
item.description: Quantum computers based on atoms could provide access to encrypted data much sooner than scientists thought.
